chapters.title: Closing the triangle
narration: The frame is done: three wedges round every one of these 40 triangles. Now close the middles, with the same wedges.

chapters.title: One wedge
narration: Here is one wedge, end on, three times life size. Its face is 4.59 inches wide. From the face to the point it is 5.54 inches deep. Deeper than it is wide.

chapters.title: A pair, points in
narration: Now a pair. Turn the second one over so the points face each other, and lay the slants together. That's a solid block, and it reaches one depth down the triangle: 5.54 inches. Its faces bear on the next pair's, and the slants are what shows.

chapters.title: Slide it to a bowtie
narration: Slide one along the other's slant. The pair reaches further down, and opens in the middle. At the end only the points touch: a bowtie. It reaches 11.1 inches, and it's half air.

chapters.title: Filled nested
narration: Fill a triangle from its top corner down, nested. Each pair is as long as the triangle is wide where it lies. 9 pairs close it: 18 wedges, 51 feet.

chapters.title: Filled bowtie
narration: The same triangle with bowtie pairs. Each one reaches twice as far, so 5 pairs close it: 10 wedges, 31 feet.

chapters.title: Side by side
narration: Side by side: the same opening, 51 feet of wedge nested, 31 as bowties.

chapters.title: The whole dome, nested
narration: Now every triangle. Nested pairs, laid from each top corner down, every wedge cut to the walls and planed flush with the frame. 800 pieces, 2,646 feet.

chapters.title: Slide them all
narration: Slide every pair at once. Nested, 800 pieces. Half slid, 580. Bowtie, 420, and 1,371 feet.

chapters.title: Dial it in each triangle
narration: Or dial it inside every triangle: nested at the top corner and along the base, where the frame carries its load, opening to bowties through the middle. 540 pieces, 1,866 feet.

chapters.title: Cut flush
narration: Close in. Every pair ends on the opening's wall in the frame's own compound cut, and both faces are planed flush with the frame. Planing takes 17% off a nested pair, 5% off a half slid one, and 1% off a bowtie.

chapters.title: The book's count
narration: The book counts its reference dome, seventy two inch chords, laid the same way. Nested: 760 wedges, 2,166 feet. Bowtie: 420 wedges, 1,292 feet.

chapters.title: In trees
narration: With the frame, the whole dome is 2,012 to 2,886 feet of wedge: 4.2 to 6.0 sixty foot pines of a foot across.

chapters.title: Two layouts, two counts
narration: The first count divided the open area by the wedge's face width. That fits a different layout: faces out, points in, each wedge covering its own face. With the points facing each other down the triangle, the reach sets the pitch. Laid pair by pair that way, nested is 2,166 feet against the first count's 2,235, and bowtie 1,292 against 1,117. Both are ideal counts, before kerf and offcuts.

chapters.title: Rings
narration: That is one family. The Triangle Infill tool knows others, and the dome wears every one. Rings: the frame repeated inward, ring by ring, in five lays: flip-flop, same hand, shimmed, standing, comb. From 270 to 1,020 pieces.

chapters.title: Parallel
narration: Parallel: runs along one edge, stepping across, every run ending in a compound cut on the walls. From 380 to 1,220 pieces.

chapters.title: Across
narration: Across: runs square to one edge, stepping along it. Short pieces, many of them: 520 to 1,720.

chapters.title: Chevron
narration: Chevron: runs along the two sides, meeting on the centre line. From 400 to 1,300 pieces.

chapters.title: Louvers
narration: Louvers: slats tilted and lapped. Covered from above, open to the air: a dome that breathes. 590 pieces, 1,892 feet.

chapters.title: Or cover it
narration: Or leave the frame open and cover it: every arrangement laid over the outside, bevelled to meet its neighbour across each seam. 16 ways, from 460 to 1,840 pieces.

chapters.title: Every fill, side by side
narration: Every fill, side by side at quarter scale: 4 with pairs, 21 with the tool's patterns. Nothing shows through any of them. The least wood that closes every triangle completely is chevron, same hand: 1,038 feet, 52% solid. Rings leave a plug to cut at each centre.

chapters.title: The dial
narration: The overlap is a dial. Nest them tight at the corners, where the loads gather. Open them in the middle, where a cavity holds insulation. A bowtie touching at its points alone doesn't keep the weather out, so test the joint before you trust the least number.

chapters.title: Do the one thing
narration: If any of this was worth your time, send it to one person who can
carry it further than I can. That is the whole ask. One share from
somebody with reach does more for this than a month of me in a field
with a chainsaw.
